2609.30768.title: Does Thinking Help Fairness? Reasoning Tokens Resolve Some Biases but Create More
2609.30768.paper_summary: Thinking in reasoning language models (RLMs) has been subject to debate on whether it resolves or amplifies bias. Prior works have shown competing conclusions in both directions. Using a within-model thinking-vs.-non-thinking ablation across QwQ-32B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, and Qwen3-32B on three high-stakes decision tasks (Adult, COMPAS, Credit), we show that thinking has an asymmetric dual effect on counterfactual fairness: it both resolves counterfactual flips produced by the non-thinking baseline and creates new flips at near-saturating model confidence. In all nine (model, dataset) combinations, the created flips outnumber the resolved flips by roughly 5 times. To explain the effect, we treat the thinking trace itself as a measurable site of fairness change and study it through two dynamic instruments: 1) We propose Counterfactual Depth Probability Gap (CDPG) to track bias evolution along thinking depth, and observe that bias propagates and amplifies with thinking. 2) We also formulate the Bias Transition Matrix (BTM) to show how predictions of counterfactual pairs change from non-thinking to thinking, and find that the asymmetric dual effect originates in the pair-state joint transition.
2609.30768.paper_summary_zh: 思考在推理語言模型（RLMs）中的作用一直受到爭議，討論它是否解決或加劇偏見。先前的研究在這兩個方向上顯示了相互競爭的結論。通過在三個高風險決策任務（成人、COMPAS、信用）上對 QwQ-32B、DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B 和 Qwen3-32B 進行模型內的思考與非思考的消融實驗，我們顯示思考對反事實公平具有不對稱的雙重影響：它既解決了非思考基線產生的反事實翻轉，又在接近飽和的模型信心下創造了新的翻轉。在所有九個（模型、數據集）組合中，創造的翻轉數量大約是解決的翻轉數量的五倍。為了解釋這一影響，我們將思考痕跡本身視為公平變化的可測量位置，並通過兩個動態工具進行研究：1）我們提出反事實深度概率差（CDPG）來追蹤思考深度上的偏見演變，並觀察到偏見隨著思考而傳播和加劇。2）我們還制定了偏見轉換矩陣（BTM），以顯示反事實對的預測如何從非思考轉變為思考，並發現不對稱的雙重影響源於對狀態的聯合轉換。
